studies.label: Main online experiment: AI textual vs AI visual concretization vs no-AI control (crowded-train ideation)
studies.cluster_se_treatment: The paper uses iteration-level OLS with clustered robust standard errors to account for ideator differences and autocorrelation among successive refinements of the same idea. Figure 3 states that each participant provided one idea, so the described clustering is at the participant level (se_basis=participant; regression.se_type=clustered_participant). Assignment itself is individual. The exact software cluster variable is not named. PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Section 5, first paragraph; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 8), Figure 3 note.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 8), Section 4.2; PDF p. 14 (printed p. 13), endnote 5
counts_source.quote: We recruited 276 U.S.-based participants ... who contributed a total of 428 idea refinements.

arms.name: Textual concretization
arms.description: After an initial idea description, the platform supplied an AI-written usage scenario of that idea. The participant refined the description and could repeat the cycle until satisfied.

arms.name: Visual concretization
arms.description: After an initial idea description, the platform supplied an AI-generated image of that idea. The participant refined the description and could repeat the cycle until satisfied.

arms.name: Control (no concretization)
arms.description: The same iterative task, with instructions to imagine the idea and its outcomes in a usage context instead of receiving an AI concretization.

studies.task: Describe and iteratively refine an idea for improving the experience on a crowded train from boarding to alighting.

ai_tool.name: gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 (textual concretizations and prompts for the image model); DALL-E 3 (visual concretizations)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 7), Section 4.1; PDF p. 14 (printed p. 13), endnote 2. Model release years are not stated.

estimates.outcome: Idea creativity (average of automated novelty and usefulness)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Creativity is the arithmetic mean of novelty and usefulness. Novelty uses all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings and three-nearest-neighbor similarity among ideas at the same refinement stage; greater distance indicates greater novelty. Usefulness averages feasibility, elaboration, and inclusivity rated by gpt-4o-2024-05-13, with three scores per iteration averaged. Creativity is z-standardized at the iteration level. PDF p. 9 (printed p. 8), Section 4.3.2; PDF p. 14 (printed p. 13), endnote 4.

regression.model: Table 2, Model (1a): OLS on idea refinements with backward-difference condition coding; condition contrasts only. Clustered robust SEs account for repeated refinements within each ideator's single idea (Section 5 and Figure 3 note).

paper_effect.standardizer: Reported percentage increase in percentile ranks of simulated adjusted predictions, relative to the visual-concretization percentile rank; not a standardized mean difference.

estimates.notes: The regression uses refinements from all study arms. n_units is the full regression observation count, not the number of observations in the two contrasted arms. The paper does not print arm-specific participant counts or the number of people in this arm pair; n_treatment, n_control, and n_total remain null. The analyzed outputs follow the initial idea descriptions and the assigned concretization or control instructions. Each person remains in one assigned condition while refining one idea, so within_person is null. The composite scores the creativity of each refinement; its embedding-based novelty component does not make it an across-people diversity outcome. Creativity is standardized at the iteration level, not across participant averages. Section 5 reports clustered robust SEs to account for ideator differences and autocorrelation among refinements of the same idea (PDF p. 10, printed p. 9). Figure 3 states that each participant provided one idea (PDF p. 9, printed p. 8), identifying this dependence as within the randomized participant. Accordingly, regression.se_type=clustered_participant and se_basis=participant. The regression observation unit remains output, and creativity remains standardized at the iteration level. The exact software clustering variable is not named; the participant-level codes follow the stated dependence structure and the one-idea-per-participant design. Alternate specifications reuse the same sample and are not independent estimates. The arm levels are the simulated adjusted predictions explicitly printed in endnote 6 for the main textual-versus-visual result, not observed descriptive means. The signed control value transcribes the words below the mean; no mean or effect was computed. The printed claim that the visual prediction is below the mean yet at the 51st percentile is internally inconsistent and is preserved, not corrected. paper_effect is the authors’ approximate percentage increase in percentile ranks, not a standardized mean difference or a percentage increase in the raw score. The directly estimated contrast is regression.coef.

The appendix remains uninspected.

The number randomized, exclusions between recruitment and analysis, arm-level randomized and analyzed counts, and two-arm participant counts are not printed. The recruitment/contribution statement supports the study-level analyzed participant count only; no arm counts are reconstructed.

The exact software clustering variable is not named. The uncertainty basis is nevertheless identified by Section 5's account of ideator-level differences and dependence among successive refinements, together with Figure 3's one-idea-per-participant design. The regression records therefore use se_basis=participant and regression.se_type=clustered_participant; the earlier provisional output coding is superseded. PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Section 5; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 8), Figure 3 note.

No observed descriptive arm means, arm SDs, or participant-level creativity SDs are printed. Endnote 6 provides simulated adjusted predictions for the main textual-versus-visual comparison; they are labeled as such in the estimate notes. The iteration-level standardization is not used to invent an SD.

The textual-versus-control coefficient, SE, confidence interval, numerical p-value or bound, and the denominator of its reported percentage increase are absent. No contrast is computed by adding backward-difference coefficients.

Endnote 6 describes its visual adjusted prediction as below the mean while labeling it with a percentile above the midpoint. The printed signed direction and percentile wording are retained without recalculation.

Online Appendix D may contain missing descriptives, and Online Appendix E3 may report separate novelty, usefulness, component outcomes, or alternate full-sample specifications. Their contents cannot be confirmed from the available article.

S2 sample size, assignment and comparison procedures, scoring method, analysis unit, and numerical statistics require the unavailable Online Appendix E2. Randomization between the separate sample and S1 arms is not established.

notes: Reconciled against the complete supplied markdown and the PDF, including the endnotes, references, and correction notice. Every cited PDF page was extracted with PyMuPDF. Table 2 was checked in PDF text and with table recovery using the text strategy. All discrepancies in extraction/diffs/c060.json and the extra Model (1c) records were adjudicated. The shared counts and classifications were checked independently of extractor agreement: Section 4.2 supports analyzed people; endnote 5 defines regression observations as refinements; Section 4.1 and Section 6.3 establish an individually randomized, between-subjects online experiment. Post-initial refinements are scored during the same session with assigned AI available, supporting with_ai, immediate, outcome_with_ai=true, and within_person=null. Section 4.3.2 supports an automated overall-creativity composite and higher_is=more_creative; Section 5 fixes unit=output. The repeated refinements do not create a randomized within-person crossover, and the novelty component does not constitute a separately reported diversity contrast. All S1-O1 arm pairs in the screening form are represented. S2-O1 is listed in not_extracted because randomization between samples is not established. No additional in-scope outcome or contrast was found in the supplied article. The textual-versus-control percentage record uses extractor A’s slug; extractor B’s reported_percentage slug is the same estimate, not a second effect. No preregistration or use of these participants by another paper is stated. Only printed numbers are recorded; no arm counts, means, SDs, contrasts, effect sizes, or uncertainty values were computed. Source quotations preserve the table’s printed precision; whitespace is normalized. Review date: 2026-10-10; extractor: reconciled. Fixer review (2026-10-10): all 593 lines of the supplied markdown, including endnotes, references, and the correction notice, were read. The flagged passages and Table 2 were checked directly with PyMuPDF. Eight flagged code fields were corrected across four regression records, with their explanatory notes and sources synchronized. The prior se_basis decisions retained in resolutions are historical and are superseded by fixes. The mechanical control_mean flag is documented in kept. All numerical statistics, counts, and other estimate classifications remain unchanged. The separate online appendix remains unavailable: there are no embedded files or matching local supplements, and fresh urllib requests to the named DOI and St. Gallen sources with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 both failed with WinError 10013.
primary_override: For alternative specifications of each regression contrast, Model (1a) is the main specification: Section 5 introduces it as the main-effects test and bases its main textual-versus-visual interpretation on it. Model (1b) is retained as the specification with controls. This identifies the main specification within each contrast, without resolving the choice between the two AI-versus-control arms.

fixes.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Section 5, first paragraph; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 8), Figure 3 note
fixes.quote: To capture differences at the ideator level and to account for potential autocorrelations at the idea level (e.g., idea refinements that reflected variations of the idea in the previous iteration), we employed clustered robust standard errors.
fixes.basis: Section 5 states that the clustered robust errors account for ideator-level differences and dependence among repeated refinements of an idea. Figure 3 states: Each participant provided one idea, and GenAI created its concretizations. Thus the described dependence is within the same randomized participant. Under the extraction-spec se_basis definition and codebook Section 10, the uncertainty basis is participant even though the regression observation unit is output. The corresponding estimate and study explanations and the provisional open item are updated; the earlier se_basis reconciliation decisions are superseded by this fix.

kept.locator: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 13), endnote 6, simulated adjusted prediction for visual concretizations
kept.quote: When simulating adjusted predictions, average ideators receiving visual concretizations generated ideas with an idea creativity score 0.06 SDs below the mean (i.e., the 51st percentile).
kept.why_the_flag_is_wrong: The printed phrase 0.06 SDs below the mean explicitly supplies the negative direction. Recording -0.06 transcribes that signed adjusted prediction; it does not calculate a new mean. The literal-number script misses a sign stated in words. The accompanying 51st-percentile statement is internally inconsistent with below the mean, but it does not justify changing the explicitly stated direction. The estimate notes already distinguish this simulated adjusted prediction from an observed arm mean.
